title: A provider event
description: One flat, self-describing object. The SAME shape is used in two places: each `data:` frame of an `agent.send` stream, and each entry of `agent.history.events`. That is deliberate — one schema pins both, so a replayed transcript and the live view cannot disagree about the same event. An event MUST be readable without the events before it. A provider that emits no `kind` at all is conformant: `{"text": "…"}` renders as plain assistant output. Clients ignore an unrecognised `kind` rather than failing.

kind.description: Absent means plain assistant text. Unrecognised values are ignored, not rejected.

text.description: The event's text. Its meaning follows `kind`: assistant output for text_delta, reasoning for thinking_delta, the final result for done, the recap body for recap_end. With no `kind` at all it is plain assistant output.

turnId.description: On turn_started, echoing the client-minted id.

at.description: ISO-8601 UTC. Omit rather than invent one.

title.description: thinking_title: the label for a reasoning block. `text` is accepted as a fallback.

thinkingId.description: Groups thinking_delta chunks with their thinking_title.

toolId.description: REQUIRED on tool_start and tool_end, and unique within the turn. Tools can overlap, so pairing by position is not available; an event without one is dropped, because an unpaired call renders as a row that never resolves.

input.description: tool_start: whatever the tool was called with. Any JSON.

ok.description: tool_end: false marks failure. ABSENT is not failure — it is the provider not saying.

output.description: tool_end: the tool's output. `text` is accepted as a fallback.

summary.description: tool_end: a one-line description of what the tool did.

recap.description: recap_end: the headline. ABSENT means no recap was produced — a turn that said nothing, or a summariser that failed — and the client then clears its indicator and paints nothing.

prompt.description: REQUIRED on turn_input_required: what to ask the user. The answer arrives as a resumed agent.send on the same turnId.

errorCode.description: Codes are STRINGS. `unauthenticated` is its own code because 'your credential is wrong' and 'the provider is down' need different words in front of the user, and once collapsed the distinction cannot be recovered.

terminalKinds.description: Exactly ONE of these ends every stream. Not referenced by validation — a single event cannot express a whole-stream rule — but named here so implementers and the conformance runner share one list.
